analysis.problem_summary: Determine the longest prefix common to all strings in an array.
analysis.intuition: Instead of comparing entire string pairs horizontally, compare characters at column index `i` across all strings. The moment any string differs at index `i`, the prefix ends immediately.
approach: Find the minimum length among all strings to bound the search.
Iterate index `i` from `0` to `minLen - 1` (column by column).
For each index `i`, iterate through all strings `j` in the array (row by row).
If `strs[j].charAt(i)` does not match `strs[0].charAt(i)`, return the substring `strs[0][0...i]` immediately.
If the outer loop finishes without mismatch, return `strs[0][0...minLen]`.
analysis.why_it_works: Vertical scanning checks candidate prefix positions in ascending order. Since a common prefix requires identical characters at every column index for all strings, the first mismatch directly defines the end of the common prefix.
analysis.key_takeaway: Vertical scanning allows early exit as soon as a character mismatch occurs at any column index, making it optimal when common prefixes are short.
analysis.time_explanation: In the worst case, every character in every string is checked, resulting in O(S) total comparisons. In practice, early exit happens as soon as a mismatch is found.
analysis.space_explanation: Only constant space is used for pointer variables and loop counters.

analysis.problem_summary: Find the longest prefix shared among all strings in an array.
analysis.intuition: The common prefix of all strings cannot be longer than the common prefix of any adjacent pair of strings. By comparing string pairs sequentially (`strs[i]` and `strs[i+1]`), we can dynamically update the maximum allowed length of the common prefix.
approach: Initialize `minLen` with the length of the first string.
Iterate through adjacent string pairs in the array from `i = 0` to `strs.length - 2`.
For each pair, iterate character by character up to the minimum length of the two strings.
Stop matching when characters differ or `minLen` bound is reached, then update `minLen` with the matched count.
Return the substring of the first string from index `0` to `minLen`.
analysis.why_it_works: The prefix property is associative: `LCP(S1, S2, S3) = LCP(LCP(S1, S2), S3)`. Thus, continuously bounding the prefix length across adjacent string comparisons guarantees the correct overall common prefix length.
analysis.key_takeaway: Sequential pairwise comparison reduces the problem to repeated two-string prefix checks, updating a single boundary variable.
analysis.time_explanation: In the worst case where all strings are identical, every character in all strings is inspected once, yielding O(S) time where S is the total number of characters across all strings.
analysis.space_explanation: Only primitive integer variables are used for index bounds, requiring O(1) auxiliary space.
